tagline: Tell us your budget. We'll tell you what to buy.

categories.name: Phones
guide: Start with the processor and the screen, not the camera megapixels. A Snapdragon 6-series, 7-series or Dimensity 7000-series chip will stay smooth for years; Unisoc and Helio chips are fine for calls, WhatsApp and YouTube but slow down with heavy apps. An AMOLED screen is the single biggest upgrade you will notice every day.

Phone prices in India went up sharply in 2026 because memory chips got more expensive, so last year's models are often the better deal. That is why many of our picks are 2025 phones still in stock at lower prices, while some newer models are listed above their old price brackets.

Check how many years of software updates the brand promises, and whether there is a service centre near you. Samsung, Motorola, OnePlus and Google are the safest for long-term support. Ignore claims like 'up to 16GB RAM' — that counts storage used as virtual RAM, not real memory.

categories.name: Laptops
guide: Look at the processor and RAM first. For college and office work, a 13th-gen Core i3, Core 3, Ryzen 3 7000 or Ryzen 5 is enough; for coding, editing or many browser tabs, get 16GB RAM and an H-series chip (like the Core i5-13420H or Core 5 210H). Always pick an SSD, and check whether the RAM can be upgraded later, because many thin laptops have it soldered.

Laptop prices in India jumped in 2026 because memory chips got more expensive, so a Core i3 laptop that used to cost around ₹35,000 now sells for ₹45,000 or more. Under ₹35k the honest choices are Chromebooks, Android-based laptops or older Windows chips. If you need Windows for Office, coding or exams, stretching to about ₹45,000 gets you a laptop that will last.

Read the warranty line before you buy: onsite warranty means a technician comes to you, carry-in means you visit a service centre. Dell, HP, Lenovo, ASUS and Acer have the widest service networks. For gaming, the graphics card matters more than the processor: an RTX 2050 is entry level, an RTX 3050 handles most games at medium settings, and RTX 50-series cards run new games at high settings.

categories.name: Earbuds
guide: Decide first whether you need active noise cancelling (ANC). It blocks bus, train and office noise and is worth it if you commute; real ANC starts around ₹1,800 now. Without ANC, spend on battery life, comfort and a known brand instead. Ignore the big 'up to 100 hours' battery claims: that number includes the case, and each charge of the buds usually lasts 5–8 hours.

Cheap earbuds fail more often. Under ₹1,500, about 13–15% of buyers on Amazon and Flipkart rate their earbuds 1–2★, mostly because one bud stops working or charging after a few months. From ₹1,600 up, OnePlus and realme models drop to around 6–10%. Paying a little more for a brand with service centres, like OnePlus, realme, boAt, Samsung or Apple, makes warranty claims much easier.

Match the earbuds to your phone. AirPods work best with iPhones and Galaxy Buds with Samsung phones; most extra features are locked to their own brand. For running or cycling outdoors, open-ear or bone-conduction designs let you hear traffic. For gaming, look for a 'low latency' or 'game' mode of 50ms or less.

categories.name: Headphones
guide: Pick the type first. Bluetooth headphones are best for phones and travel; wired headphones never need charging, last for years and give better sound for the money; gaming headsets add a boom mic for team chat. Over-ear cups are more comfortable for long hours than on-ear ones, which press on your ears.

If you commute or work in a noisy place, get noise cancelling (ANC). The boAt Rockerz 512 ANC is the cheapest one we trust, the Sony WH-CH720N and JBL Tune 780NC are the sweet spot, and the Sony WH-1000XM5 and Bose QuietComfort are the best. If you record music or edit video, choose studio headphones like the Audio-Technica ATH-M20x or Sony MDR-7506: they sound flat and accurate rather than bassy.

Check the battery number honestly: 30–50 hours is plenty for most people, and anything over 60 hours usually means lower volume or ANC off. Sony, JBL, boAt and Bose have the widest service networks in India. For gaming on a PC or console, wired headsets from HyperX or Razer are more reliable and cheaper than wireless ones.

categories.name: Earphones
guide: Check your phone's port before buying wired earphones. Most new phones have no 3.5mm headphone jack, so you need a Type-C pair (or an adapter). Wired earphones are still the best value for calls, online classes and gaming, because they have no delay and no battery to wear out.

Neckbands sit between wired earphones and earbuds: they are hard to lose, last 25–40 hours and cost less than good earbuds. OnePlus and realme make the most reliable ones. If you want noise cancelling on a budget, a neckband like the realme Buds Wireless 5 ANC is cheaper than ANC earbuds.

For better music, look at in-ear monitors (IEMs) like the KZ EDC Pro or ZSN Pro X. They sound far clearer than typical earphones at the same price, but KZ is an imported brand sold through resellers, so service is limited. Cheap earphones under ₹500 wear out within a year for about 1 in 8 buyers, so treat them as replaceable.
